Research / biology

Microbial evolution

Evolutionary dynamics of microbial populations and communities

All research↗

Overview

Microbial evolution operates at extraordinary speeds, making microbes ideal systems for studying evolutionary processes in real-time. Our research examines how bacteria, archaea, viruses, and fungi evolve in response to environmental pressures, competition, and cooperation within complex communities.

Questions we explore.

01

Experimental Evolution

Using laboratory evolution experiments to observe adaptation, mutation accumulation, and evolutionary innovation in real-time

02

Microbial Community Dynamics

Modeling ecological and evolutionary interactions within microbiomes and their impact on host health

03

Horizontal Gene Transfer

Investigating how genetic exchange between microbes accelerates adaptation and spreads traits like antibiotic resistance

04

Metabolic Evolution

Understanding how microbial metabolic networks evolve to exploit new resources and environmental niches

05

Viral-Host Coevolution

Studying the evolutionary arms race between bacteriophages and their bacterial hosts

Methods & perspective.

We combine experimental evolution with high-throughput genomic sequencing, metagenomics, and computational modeling. Our work integrates population genetics theory with systems biology to predict evolutionary trajectories and understand the genetic basis of adaptation.

Research directions

Antibiotic Resistance Evolution

Tracking the emergence and spread of resistance mechanisms in bacterial populations under different treatment regimens

Microbiome Assembly Rules

Determining how evolutionary and ecological processes shape the composition and function of microbial communities

Synthetic Microbial Consortia

Engineering stable microbial communities for biotechnology applications using evolutionary principles
